issues.title: Storage layer: add `consumed` IndexedDB object store
issues.body:
## Summary
Add a new IndexedDB object store `consumed` parallel to the existing `watchlist`/`disliked`/`history`. Five new exports. Bump `DB_VERSION` 2 → 3 with a safe migration.

**Files:** `js/storage.js`
**Effort:** S (1-2h)
**Dependencies:** None (foundation — unblocks LIB-002, LIB-010, LIB-011).

## What to do
- Add exports: `getConsumed`, `addToConsumed`, `removeFromConsumed`, `updateConsumedRating`, `getAllConsumedIds`
- Bump `DB_VERSION` 2 → 3; add a `consumed` store with `keyPath: 'id'` in the `onupgradeneeded` handler
- Migration must preserve existing `watchlist` / `disliked` / `history` data
- `updateConsumedRating(id, rating)` updates only the `consumedRating` field, leaves everything else
- `getAllConsumedIds()` returns a `Set<string>` for use in dedup

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Existing IndexedDB data preserved on upgrade from v2 → v3
- [ ] `consumed` store created with keyPath `id`
- [ ] `getConsumed()` returns all items as an array (or `[]` if none)
- [ ] `addToConsumed(item)` and `removeFromConsumed(id)` round-trip cleanly
- [ ] `updateConsumedRating(id, rating)` updates only the `consumedRating` field
- [ ] `getAllConsumedIds()` returns a `Set<string>`

## Tests required
`tests/library-storage.test.js` — CRUD, migration from v2, empty-store behavior, rating update.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Storage layer (js/storage.js)" and §LIB-001.

issues.title: Atomic add-consumed helper (`_addConsumedAtomic`)
issues.body:
## Summary
Single canonical helper `_addConsumedAtomic(item, rating)` that handles conflict detection + atomic write for ALL add-consumed flows (modal, kebab promote, quick-promote from want-to).

**Files:** `js/app.js` (new method on `App`)
**Effort:** M (3-6h)
**Dependencies:** LIB-001. Stubs the LIB-012 `BroadcastChannel` call.

## What to do
- Read `watchlist` and `consumed` in one transaction
- Detect conflicts (in both, or already consumed) and call a UI prompt
- Write/delete in a single `readwrite` transaction
- Return the final stored item (or a `{ status: 'already-exists' }` sentinel)
- Idempotent: calling twice with the same item is safe

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Adding an item not in watchlist → stored in `consumed`, no watchlist change
- [ ] Adding an item in watchlist → prompt appears; "Move it" deletes from watchlist, "Add separately" leaves it
- [ ] Adding an item already consumed → returns `already-exists`, no write
- [ ] BroadcastChannel call is stubbed (deferred to LIB-012)
- [ ] Idempotent under double-tap

## Tests required
`tests/library-atomic.test.js` — all 4 conflict scenarios, idempotency.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Resolved design decisions" #1 (Race condition) and §LIB-002.

issues.title: Recommender: add `updateFromConsumed` with 1.2x/1.5x weighting
issues.body:
## Summary
New `Recommender.updateFromConsumed(item, rating)` with rating-modulated weighting. Rating 3 is neutral; 4-5 are positive; 1-2 are negative. No decay (consumed is a permanent signal).

**Files:** `js/recommender.js`
**Effort:** M (3-6h)
**Dependencies:** None. Modify `rebuildProfile()` to iterate `consumed` items too.

## Weighting spec
| Rating | Weight | Equivalent to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | -1.5x | "nope" swipe + half a "skip" |
| 2 | -0.75x | "nope" swipe (half strength) |
| 3 | 0x | "skip" (neutral) |
| 4 | +1.2x | "like" swipe |
| 5 | +1.5x | "like" swipe + half a second like |

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `updateFromConsumed(item, 5)` ≈ two right-swipes on the same item
- [ ] `updateFromConsumed(item, 1)` ≈ a "nope" + a "skip"
- [ ] `updateFromConsumed(item, 3)` leaves the taste vector unchanged
- [ ] `rebuildProfile()` correctly loads consumed items from storage
- [ ] Existing swipe-based recommendations are NOT regressed (regression test)
- [ ] Consumed items do NOT touch the decay system

## Tests required
`tests/library-recommender.test.js` (covered also by LIB-014) — all 5 rating levels, profile rebuild, regression vs swipe behavior.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Recommender signal weighting" and §LIB-010.

issues.title: Kebab popover menu (with viewport-aware positioning)
issues.body:
## Summary
Popover menu that opens on kebab tap. Viewport-aware positioning. Closes on click-outside, Escape, or action selection.

**Files:** `js/app.js` (new `_showKebabMenu(cardEl, item, status)`), `css/styles.css`
**Effort:** M (3-6h)
**Dependencies:** LIB-004 (uses the kebab button), LIB-006 ("I finished this" action).

## Actions per status
**Want to card:**
1. "I finished this →" (primary, weight 600) — opens rating modal (LIB-006)
2. "Open detail" (secondary) — opens existing card modal
3. "Remove from Want to" (destructive, red) — deletes from watchlist

**Consumed card:**
1. "Update rating" (primary) — re-opens rating modal with current rating pre-filled
2. "Open detail" (secondary)
3. "Remove from library" (destructive) — deletes from consumed, recommender forgets it

## Positioning logic
- Kebab in left half of viewport → popover opens to the RIGHT
- Kebab in right half → popover opens to the LEFT
- Card near bottom → popover opens UPWARD
- Z-index 100, closes on click-outside / Escape / action / scroll

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Popover opens within 100ms of kebab click
- [ ] Position adapts per the rules above (no edge clipping)
- [ ] All 3 actions per status route correctly
- [ ] Destructive action shows confirm toast with 3-second Undo window
- [ ] Keyboard: arrow keys move focus, Enter activates
- [ ] Mobile: popover becomes full-width bottom sheet

## Tests required
`tests/library-kebab.test.js` — positioning, action routing, keyboard, mobile sheet mode.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Long-press / kebab menu discoverability" and §LIB-005.

issues.title: Add Consumed modal (search → results → 5-star rating)
issues.body:
## Summary
Modal opened from the Library page's "+ Add consumed" button. Three internal states: search (with recents + quick-promote from Want to), results, rating.

**Files:** `js/app.js` (new `_showAddConsumedModal(app)`), `css/styles.css`
**Effort:** L (1-2 days)
**Dependencies:** LIB-001, LIB-002, LIB-009.

## The 3 states

### Search state
- Search input, autofocus, debounced 350ms
- Recent searches from localStorage (max 5)
- Quick-promote row: watchlist thumbnails (up to 8); tap = opens rating modal directly

### Results state
- List of search results (uses existing search APIs: OpenLibrary + Google Books for books, TMDB multi for movies/TV, IGDB for games)
- Each result has a `+ Mark as consumed` button on the right

### Rating state
- Centered thumbnail + title + year
- 5 large star selector, default 4 stars, hover preview, click to fill
- CTA text reflects current rating: "Mark as consumed (4 stars) ✓"
- CTA disabled until 1+ stars selected
- Optional Steam playtime note for games (if user has Steam integrated)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Search input has autofocus on open
- [ ] Results appear within 500ms (debounced 350ms)
- [ ] Recent searches persist in localStorage (max 5)
- [ ] Quick-promote shows up to 8 watchlist thumbnails
- [ ] Star selector: hover preview, click fills, CTA reflects rating
- [ ] CTA disabled until 1+ stars selected
- [ ] Steam playtime (games only) shown read-only when available
- [ ] Closes on Escape, X button, click-outside

## Tests required
`tests/library-add-modal.test.js` — debounce, recents persistence, star interaction, CTA enable/disable, Steam playtime.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Add as consumed flow" and §LIB-006.

issues.title: Discover dedup: hide consumed items from swipe deck
issues.body:
## Summary
Add a third lookup set alongside `watchIds` and `dislikedIds` in the discover filter chain. Consumed items should NEVER appear in the swipe deck, period.

**Files:** `js/app.js` (modify `renderDiscover`, `_refillDeck`, `_fetchGenreRotation`)
**Effort:** S (1-2h)
**Dependencies:** LIB-001 (consumed store), LIB-010 (recommender integration).

## What to do
```js
const consumedIds = new Set(this.consumed.map(c => c.id));
let filtered = items.filter(i =>
  !watchIds.has(i.id) &&
  !dislikedIds.has(i.id) &&
  !consumedIds.has(i.id)
);
```
Apply at all three filter points: `renderDiscover`, `_refillDeck` (watchlist-based refill), `_fetchGenreRotation` (local-sources refill).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Items in `consumed` never appear in the swipe deck
- [ ] Items in `consumed` never appear in the genre-rotation refill
- [ ] Items in `consumed` never appear in the local-sources refill
- [ ] No regression for items NOT in `consumed`
- [ ] Cold start works (empty `consumed` set → no impact)

## Tests required
`tests/library-dedup.test.js` — all three filter points.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Discover view dedup" and §LIB-011.

issues.title: Cross-tab sync via `BroadcastChannel('bookswipe-library')`
issues.body:
## Summary
Wire up the `BroadcastChannel` stub that LIB-002 added. When tab A adds/removes/updates a library item, tab B re-fetches its state and re-renders the affected view.

**Files:** `js/app.js` (new `_initLibraryBroadcast()` called from `App` constructor)
**Effort:** S (1-2h)
**Dependencies:** LIB-002 (the atomic helper stubs the broadcast call).

## What to do
- Create a `BroadcastChannel('bookswipe-library')` in the `App` constructor
- On message: re-fetch `this.watchlist` and `this.consumed`, re-render the Library page (if active)
- On `beforeunload`: close the channel
- Wrap all `BroadcastChannel` calls in try/catch — silent failure if the browser doesn't support it

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add in tab A → tab B's Library page shows the new item within 1 second
- [ ] Remove in tab A → tab B removes it
- [ ] In-flight add-consumed modal in one tab is NOT interrupted by the other tab
- [ ] Channel errors are caught and logged (no uncaught exceptions)
- [ ] Channel closed on `beforeunload`

## Tests required
`tests/library-broadcast.test.js` — multi-tab sync, error handling, cleanup.

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §"Race condition" (decision 1) and §LIB-012.

issues.title: Recommender tests: `updateFromConsumed` + integration
issues.body:
## Summary
Unit + integration tests for the recommender's new `updateFromConsumed` method.

**Files:** `tests/recommender-consumed.test.js` (new)
**Effort:** M (3-6h)
**Dependencies:** LIB-010.

## Unit tests (5 rating levels)
- [ ] 1-star → taste vector shifts away from item's genres
- [ ] 2-star → taste vector shifts away (slightly less)
- [ ] 3-star → taste vector unchanged
- [ ] 4-star → taste vector shifts toward item's genres (1.2x)
- [ ] 5-star → taste vector shifts toward item's genres (1.5x)
- [ ] Multiple consumed items: vectors combine correctly
- [ ] Mixed consumed + swipe signals: both contribute
- [ ] `rebuildProfile()` correctly merges consumed items

## Integration tests
- [ ] Adding a 5-star consumed item increases the like rate for similar items by >10%
- [ ] Adding a 1-star consumed item decreases the like rate for similar items by >10%

## Regression
- [ ] Existing recommender behavior unchanged when `consumed` is empty

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All 5 rating levels tested
- [ ] Profile rebuild tested
- [ ] Integration test shows measurable like-rate change (use synthetic data)
- [ ] Regression test passes

## Source of truth
`library-spec.md` §LIB-014 and §"Telemetry for tuning" (the A/B test plan in decision #8).
